title: Sephiria Wishing Fountain — Town Artifact Picker
description: Sephiria wishing fountain guide: unlock via Destiny New Events, pick town Artifacts for the next run, and how Willpower expands capacity.
meta: Town pre-run Artifact picker; capacity figures are community-reported and should be checked in-game.
sources: YT: intro tips (wishing well / artifact favorites)
body:
The Sephiria Wishing Fountain in town is easy to miss: it is a pre-run Artifact picker, not the dungeon interactable whose water changes color.

The same object is also searched as the “fountain of wishes” or the wishing well — all three point to the town Artifact picker described below.

What it does

Once unlocked, you select Artifacts in Bunnyville and carry those picks into the next dungeon run. Intro footage treats this as the “wishing well” step after you decide a weapon / combo family.

Confirm the picks only after that family is chosen. A summoner start spends the slots on Companion-tagged Artifacts — the Companion build is the pick list. Higher rarity is reported to cost more of the bar, so one expensive Artifact can use up the default capacity of 4 and leave the rest of the set for the dungeon.

Wish in Bunnyville after the family is locked and before you enter the dungeon. The bar is one pre-run set; it does not restock on a floor. If capacity is still small, take the single Artifact that fits the family and leave the rest of the set for dungeon offers.

How you unlock it

Open it through New Events on Destiny Inscription—the same early spends that unlock the costume salon and extra weapons. See the beginner guide.

Capacity

  • A community talent writeup reports a default capacity of 4; verify the current value in-game.
  • Willpower expands it: +1 at talent Lv5 and +4 at Lv20, for a reported maximum of 9; verify this against your current talent levels. A 1.0 tips video also treats Willpower as the stat that changes fountain / dice quality.
  • A community writeup reports that higher rarity costs more capacity (Common 3 / Advanced 4 / Rare 5 / Legendary 6). Confirm the current bars in-client; these figures may have changed.

The same talent writeup turns those costs into a pick. At the reported default of 4 you can take one Common (one point left unused) or one Advanced (the bar is full). A Rare fits once capacity is 5, which that writeup ties to Willpower Lv5. At the reported maximum of 9 that writeup lists three Commons, two Advanced (one point left unused), a Rare plus a Common (one point left unused), a Rare plus an Advanced, or a Legendary plus a Common. Match the bars on your fountain before you lock a Legendary.

Do not mix this up with in-dungeon fountains that can grant XP, gold, or spawn enemies when the water changes color. Those are a different object.

For optional dungeon rewards after a run begins, see how to find Sephiria secret rooms. Related: Companion build (start with the Companion family) · Destiny / talents · Artifacts · Builds.

Picking Artifacts only pays off if they are actually active in your run: items in the Side Bag stay inactive, including Tablets. During a run, secret-room cracks are a separate source of supplies.
